note: A sealed station with more domes (the moon) adds a pin for its landing bay and one per dome ('bay', 'barracks', 'homes': GlobeMap.station_pins; the barracks' says who holds it), and the globe draws the station's domes, pit and tunnels as outlines under them (GlobeMap.station_shapes). The F11 Map page (src/systems/flow/globe_map.gd, src/ui/globe_view.gd): a globe of the planet with the places that stay put, each clickable to set a waypoint the HUD's objective pointer follows. Pins come from the world's landmarks (the Remnant's outposts and the port also say who holds them: Territory; 'held' lines are their hover text, 'legend_' lines the legend's) (content/core/worlds/), the planet's native camps and the town's markers, and vehicles: they move and are on it too (GlobeMap.vehicles: your ships and speeders, the Remnant's ships while they fly and, while they hold the town, their speeders, and the rival racers while a race runs; kinds 'ship_yours', 'speeder_yours', 'ship_enemy', 'speeder_enemy', 'speeder_rival', named 'your_vehicle' / 'enemy_vehicle' / 'rival_vehicle'; each drawn as its own silhouette, its ship or vehicle file's 'icon'): while the Map page is open they move on it every 'vehicle_refresh_s' seconds (a ship you called keeps flying to you), and one picked as the waypoint is followed wherever it goes ('vehicle:<id>'). Every row of the legend is a button: a click centres the globe on the next place of that kind and sets the waypoint there ('legend_count' / 'legend_at' say how many and which). 'kinds' names each landmark kind ('location' landmarks use their location file's kind); a location's own 'label' wins over the kind's, and 'labels' wins over both. 'skip' lists landmark ids left off. 'town' are the port's own stops (a 'marker' where it stands, or a 'zone': the middle of its biggest block, the barracks, who holds it said as the port's is), shown once zoomed in past 'town_zoom' or the town is big enough on screen (content/look/map.json 'details'; the port's pin hides then); the town's vendors (content/core/vendors/) are added to them, each named by 'vendor_kinds' (by vendor id), else a 'wares_kinds' kind for what its stall shows (content/look/items.json 'stalls'), and every free market stall (issue #147, CommunityNpc) as 'free_stall' ('build_npc': 'Build an NPC') or, once someone keeps it, 'keeper' with the keeper's name (yours from the builder's draft until it is merged). The ranches' stands show the same way once a ranch is zoomed into. The cantina owner's pin is 'owner_named' once this save has named them. 'arrive' is how close (m) counts as there: the waypoint clears itself. 'off_planet' heads the list of places beside the map: the star system's chart (src/ui/system_view.gd: every planet where it really hangs, the home planet in the middle; 'system_' lines), every planet in it (this one marked 'system_here'), and every Remnant cruiser in the system ('cruiser_over': named by the planet it hangs over); clicking one opens its own map (another planet's globe, or that cruiser's side view with 'cruiser_places' named; a waypoint set there leads to its planet first). On the system's chart each cruiser is a small badge (the 'cruiser' pin shape: the ship side on, in a dark frame) coloured by who holds it, hovered it names the ship and says where it is and who holds it ('cruiser_at', 'cruiser_remnant', 'cruiser_locals', 'cruiser_empty'), and a click opens its side view, and 'back' returns to this one. The page opens on the planet you are on, and on the system's chart out in space (above the planet's space_altitude in a ship). A waypoint set on another planet points there first ('waypoint_there'). Looks: content/look/map.json.
